questions.q: What does a multimeter read between CAN_H and CAN_L on a healthy bus with the power off?
questions.explain: Two 120 Ω terminators at the ends in parallel give 60 Ω; 120 means one terminator, 40 means three.

questions.q: Why does CAN tolerate a meter of wire next to the power bus while I²C does not?
options: CAN runs at a higher frequency and has time to retransmit the frame
CAN is differential: the interference is the same on both wires
CAN is shielded inside the connector
questions.explain: The receiver looks at the difference H−L; common-mode interference cancels out.

questions.q: A new DroneCAN node was connected without any setup and it worked. Who gave it its ID?
options: The DNA server on the flight controller
The ID is burned in at the factory and never changes
questions.explain: Dynamic node allocation: the flight controller hands out a free node ID and remembers it against the node's unique ID.

questions.q: After moving a GPS node from another aircraft, the GPS data jumps. The likely cause?
options: No terminator at the flight controller
questions.explain: The stored ID matches another node; the cure is clearing the DNA database or changing the ID.

questions.q: Which ArduPilot parameter selects DroneCAN as the protocol of the first driver?
questions.explain: CAN_P1_DRIVER enables the port and assigns the driver; CAN_D1_PROTOCOL = 1 selects DroneCAN for that driver.

questions.q: The nodes are visible in Mission Planner, but the EKF gets no GPS. What do you check first?
options: The node firmware version in the list
questions.explain: A node on the bus does not mean the autopilot uses it as a GPS; the sensor type is selected explicitly.

questions.q: Eight ESCs on CAN at 400 Hz plus sensors: what is the sensible thing to do?
options: Raise the bus bit rate to 2 Mbit/s on all nodes at once
Move the ESCs to a separate CAN2 bus
Remove the terminators to reduce the load
questions.explain: ESC commands take a noticeable share of the bandwidth; two buses split the load and give a backup.
